To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

GLT-1 is a key regulator of glutamate levels in the synaptic cleft, and that disruption of GL-1 by DHK inhibits the tetanically sciatically stimulation-induced long-term potentiation and Fos expression of spinal nociception neurons.

the inhibition of glutamate transporter GL-T 1 by DHK may be associated with an accumulation of extracytoplasmic glutamate and the inhibition of functional expression of Fos protein in spinal neurons, but not with neuronal apoptosis.

the inhibition of spinal LTP by disrupting GLT-1 was related to the accumulation of glutamate in the extracellular space, which may be associated with functional activation of spinal nociceptors expressing Fos.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new mechanism of central sensitization, which may have important implications in the pathogenesis of neuropathic pain.
the role of GLT- in the tetanically sciati stimulation-induced LTP in the spinal dorsal horn.
the role of glutamate transporters in synaptic plasticity and the pathogenesis of central sensitization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inhibition of GLT- 1 function may be a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of chronic pain.
glial glutamate transporters play an important role, but not the only role, in tetanically evoked spinal LTP.
the spinal glutamate transporter GL-1 is an important regulator of spinal nociception and central sensitization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glial GLT1 may serve as a regulator of synaptic plasticity of spinal nociception.

GLT-1 is an essential component for the induction and/or maintenance of tetanically evoked spinal LTP and that this LTP may be a substrate of inflammation- and nerve injury-induced central sensitization.
GLT-1 is a critical factor in regulating synaptic glutamate levels and the functional activation of spinal nociceptors, which is important in nociception and neuropathic pain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GLT-1 is important in regulating the excitability of spinal neurons and the expression of Fos.
the glutamate transporter GLAST is important in the regulation of glutamate in the spinal cord, and that it is involved in the regulation of synaptic plasticity in the spinal cord.
glutamate transporters may be an important regulator of spinal nociception.
